Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
17 October 2026 .
Brent $ 109.69 + 3.56 % · Transits 2 (2026-10-11) · AI-assisted
01 Al Jazeera and the Straits Times report Houthis fired two missiles at Aden airport, with the Saudi-led coalition intercepting a missile headed for Yanbu.

02 Iranian state media claim a supertanker struck a naval mine in the Strait of Hormuz and caught fire; no maritime authority has confirmed the incident.

03 Moneycontrol reports 15 Indian crew aboard oil tanker MT ST 3 are safe after the vessel was hit by a projectile in the strait, reported on October 14; Newsquawk reports an Indian shipping official says a crude oil tanker was targeted by a missile.

Situation
The Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed to commercial traffic, with IMF PortWatch recording 2 transits on October 11 against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day. Attacks on shipping continue on multiple fronts: Iranian state media claim a supertanker struck a naval mine and caught fire in the strait, while Al Jazeera relays the IRGC's account without independently corroborating it. Separately, Moneycontrol reports 15 Indian crew aboard oil tanker MT ST 3 are safe after a projectile strike, reported on October 14, and Newsquawk reports an Indian shipping official says a crude oil tanker was targeted by a missile in the strait. Iran's navy says additional tankers it describes as "violating" have caught fire east of the strait; no major wire in this feed carries those claims independently. CNBC reports Singapore-flagged ships have been attacked in the strait, with FreightWaves and Yahoo both reporting container ship attacks escalating. On the second front, Al Jazeera and the Straits Times report the Houthis fired two missiles at Aden airport, with the Saudi-led coalition intercepting a missile headed for Yanbu, extending the pattern of strikes on Arabian Peninsula infrastructure seen since October 10. The feed indexed 56 headlines in the last 24 hours. Brent settled at $109.69 at Friday's close, up 3.56% in that session; WTI stood at $101.84. As of 03:22 UTC, 157 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, a count that leaves out ships within 25km of a working port. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the high band, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.
